claim: One click opens a filled cart-loop practice with sample history.
sandbox: fresh browser context at /; click the first-screen sample action and assert /?demo=1, the demo banner, seeded hypothesis, and sample history

claim: Reset demo restores the shipped sample, and leaving the demo clears its keys.
where: demo banner, privacy page, demo documentation
sandbox: fresh browser context at /?demo=1; edit and reset, assert the shipped sample, then leave through Home and assert no localStorage keys remain

claim: The VS Code extension records a hypothesis, test output, fix, and clue in a debugging receipt.
sandbox: fresh VS Code user-data and extensions directories; activate the packaged extension, open its contributed view, save all four fields, and inspect local extension state

claim: The VS Code extension can delete all saved receipts after a specific confirmation.
where: privacy page, VS Code receipt view
sandbox: fresh VS Code profile; save a receipt to local extension state, clear it through the extension API used by the confirmed view action, and assert zero receipts

claim: The separate Chrome extension records the same four receipt fields in a browser popup.
sandbox: fresh Chromium extension profile; load the packaged MV3 extension, complete all four fields, save, inspect, export, and delete the receipt

claim: The practice asks for a testable hypothesis before test output or a fix.
sandbox: fresh browser context at /?demo=1; assert the test field is absent until the hypothesis is locked

claim: Website demo entries stay in the separate demo browser namespace.
where: demo banner, privacy page, demo documentation
sandbox: fresh browser context at /?demo=1; complete a receipt while recording requests and inspect demo-only localStorage keys

claim: VS Code receipts use local extension storage and are not sent over the network.
where: landing facts, privacy page, VS Code extension, README
sandbox: fresh VS Code profile; save a unique receipt, inspect global extension state, and scan the packaged extension for network clients or endpoints

claim: The website demo works offline after the first visit.
sandbox: fresh browser context at /?demo=1; wait for service worker, reload once under control, set offline, and reload

claim: A completed receipt exports as Markdown.
where: demo, VS Code and Chrome receipt actions, README
sandbox: fresh VS Code profile; save a receipt, export through the same file writer used by the view, and assert the Markdown contains all four sections; browser suites cover both web surfaces

claim: The VS Code and Chrome extensions are free to download.
sandbox: built site; request the public VSIX and Chrome ZIP without login or payment, then verify both ZIP signatures

claim: The Chrome extension requests browser storage only and has no tab or file access.
sandbox: built extension; inspect the MV3 manifest and assert storage is the only requested permission

claim: The Chrome extension has no tab, history, clipboard, or host permission and sends no receipt content over the network.
sandbox: fresh Chromium extension profile; assert all permission surfaces are storage-only, scan the packaged bundle for private-data APIs, complete a uniquely marked receipt while recording requests, and assert no HTTP request or receipt value leaves the extension

claim: The VS Code extension does not read workspace files, open editors, or clipboard contents.
sandbox: built VSIX; inspect the bundled extension and assert it has no workspace-file, document, editor, clipboard-read, process-spawn, or network-read path

claim: Neither extension generates code or answers.
sandbox: built VS Code and Chrome extensions; assert their bundles contain no model gateway, model SDK, or model endpoint

claim: The product has no analytics or third-party runtime scripts.
sandbox: fresh browser context; load landing and demo, record all requests, and inspect every runtime script source
